environment: Node 22.14 and PostgreSQL 17.11 using private local fixtures
observations: An actual pre-switch PostgreSQL dump was restored into a separate local database. Two archived deletions had completed on the original source, one on each side of the signed rollover.
A truncated window was rejected before staging any plan. The application login CONNECT grant blocked planning until it was revoked.
The manifest and ordered segment plans were immutable. A direct attempt to register the later segment before the earlier erasure failed at the SQL boundary.
The gate stayed closed after the first segment. A single-archive invocation could not substitute its completed gate for the staged window.
Both replay batches erased their exact targets, blocked both erased identities and preserved the unrelated member. Repeat plan and replay produced no new effects.
The completed window allowed a synthetic probe with the source origin still fenced and required provider reconciliation. Neither restored job was recorded as provider-deleted.
scope: The fixture used a real PostgreSQL dump, original and quarantine databases, signed archives, role checks and the owner CLI. The live deletion provider was simulated.
This drill used exact preimages from a pre-deletion backup. Hosted backup and provider reconciliation remain separate release work.
The optional billing PostgreSQL unit skip is covered by the shared integration suite.
